purpose: Implementation contract for a continuously running, leakage-resistant strategy research and evaluation engine.
required_principles: A catalogue item is a hypothesis/specification, not evidence of edge or permission to trade.
Keep detector, context filter, confirmation, entry, sizing, stop, exit and execution-cost models separate.
Every signal must store first_knowable_at, source bar timestamp, data version, code commit and full parameter JSON.
All pivots and higher-timeframe bars become available only after confirmation/close; never backdate.
Use point-in-time universes and corporate-action-adjusted data; avoid survivorship and delisting bias.
Use chronological train/validation/untouched test splits and nested walk-forward evaluation.
Track the number of strategy variants tried; use multiple-testing controls and deflated/adjusted performance statistics where appropriate.
Include brokerage, taxes/fees, spread, slippage, market impact, lot size, tick size, liquidity, circuits and realistic fills.
Report long/short separately, market/session regimes, instrument, timeframe and liquidity buckets.
Persist failed experiments; never silently discard weak or losing results.
Do not optimise on the final holdout. Re-open holdout only under a new dated research version.
Promotion to paper trading requires minimum trade count, stable out-of-sample results, robustness tests and operational checks.

validation_protocol.baseline: Buy-and-hold / benchmark and simple naive baselines, plus randomised-entry baseline with matched holding/turnover constraints.
validation_protocol.chronological_split: Example only: 60% train, 20% validation, 20% untouched test; choose dates before research and preserve a final holdout.
validation_protocol.walk_forward: Rolling or anchored windows; refit thresholds/model only on past data; evaluate next unseen block.
validation_protocol.robustness: Nearby parameter values, nearby instruments, nearby timeframes, alternate market regimes, costs doubled, delayed entries and missed fills.
validation_protocol.minimum_evidence: Define minimum trade counts and confidence intervals by strategy frequency before evaluation; do not use one universal minimum.

daily_cycle: update point-in-time features and completed-bar signals
run scheduled walk-forward folds and parameter robustness tests
recompute metrics with current cost model
compare against baselines and prior versions
write experiment ledger and immutable logs
publish leaderboard with confidence and sample size
alert on data drift, performance decay or operational failures
